title: Egress shielding and warm-pool failover playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This runbook describes detection, automatic mitigation, and manual response patterns for two correlated failure modes: (A) user-facing egress failures (egress proxy/authz/NAT exhaustion) and (B) warm-pool depletion for GPU inference tenants. These failures commonly cascade: loss of egress routing can cause warm-pool orchestrator heartbeats to stall, causing warm pools to be evicted and increasing cold-starts. The goal is to keep customer P95 inference latency and success-rate within SLOs while reducing blast radius and recovery time.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: all Redwood-hosted GPU regions and the egress fabric (egress-fabric-proxy, shared-nat-operator, egress-sidecar). Includes warm-pool-orchestrator, burst-allocator, and tenant-egress-shaper components.
- Audience: Oncall infra (network/gpu), SREs, platform engs, and incident commanders for production GPU inference.

Owners and contacts:
- Primary owner: Platform SRE (team: eng-sre)
- Secondary owner: GPU Fleet (team: eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity)
- Pager: #infra-oncall (Slack)
- Pager rotation lead: Miguel Alvarez

SLOs and thresholds referenced:
- Inference P95 latency (regional): target <= 150ms for small-chat route; alert at > 250ms for 10m.
- Token success-rate: target >= 99.5%; alert if < 98% for 5m.
- Warm-pool availability: target >= 90% of reserved warm slots; alert if < 75% for 10m.

Detection and monitoring (what to watch):
1) Synthetic probes: regional egress synthetic HTTP probes (every 15s) to /health/egress-probe through egress-fabric-proxy.
2) Telemetry dashboards:
   - egress-proxy: error-rate, tcp-reset-rate, nat-connection-saturation, 95th latency
   - warm-pool-orchestrator: connected-hosts, heartbeat-latency, eviction-rate, cold-starts/min
   - token-billing/ingress: sudden drop in request rate with rising errors (correlation)
3) Alert rules (examples):
   - EGRESS_HIGH_ERROR: egress-proxy.error_rate > 2.0% for 5m
   - WARMPOOL_DEPLETION: warm-pool.available_slots/total_reserved < 0.75 for 10m
   - SYNTH_FAIL_CORRELATION: synthetic.egress_failures > 5 in 5m AND warm-pool.evictions > 10 in 5m

Immediate automated mitigations (run automatically via orchestration playbooks):
- If EGRESS_HIGH_ERROR triggers:
  - route policy: shift 30% of traffic for non-SLA customers to regional egress fallback (policy: egress-shielding -> fallback-egress-1).
  - increase synthetic probe frequency from 15s to 5s for the affected region to gather finer telemetry.
  - temporarily relax warm-pool scale-down: set warm-pool-orchestrator.min_idle_time = 15m and suspend preemptive-eviction job.

Manual response (incident commander + oncall):
1) Triage (first 10 minutes)
   - Confirm alerts on PagerDuty and open incident channel (Slack: #incident-<region>-egress).
   - Correlate egress and warm-pool dashboards. Run correlation queries:
     - kibana query: service:egress-proxy AND status:5xx AND @timestamp:[now-10m TO now]
     - prometheus: increase(warm_pool_evictions_total[10m])
   - Assign roles: Incident Commander (IC), Network Lead, GPU Lead, Communications.

2) Containment (10–30 minutes)
   - If egress NAT exhaustion suspected: enable egress-shielding (playbook action):
     - kubectl apply -f /opt/runbooks/egress-shielding/fallback-routes.yaml
     - CLI: kubectl -n egress scale deploy/egress-fabric-proxy --replicas=3
     - Ensure shared-nat-operator has extra ephemeral IPs: run terraform apply on module terraform/modules/egress/allocate_extra_ips.tf (see below snippet).
   - If warm-pool heartbeats failing: set warm-pool-orchestrator.safety_mode = "suspend_evictions" via the runtime API: POST https://orchestrator.internal/api/v1/safety?suspend=true
   - Start eviction backfill: run the backfill job in batch cluster: airflow dags trigger warm_pool_backfill_v2

3) Remediation (30–120 minutes)
   - For transient egress proxy overloads: add capacity to egress-proxy autoscaler config and gradually shift traffic back from fallbacks:
     - edit HPA: kubectl -n egress patch hpa/egress-fabric-proxy -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":3,"maxReplicas":12}}'
   - For NAT/ENI exhaustion on cloud provider: request additional IP pool via cloud console or run terraform subcommand: 
     - terraform workspace select prod-us-west-2
     - terraform apply -target=module.egress.allocate_extra_ips -var='requested_ips=64'
   - For warm-pool orchestration bugs: increase orchestrator log level and collect traces:
     - kubectl -n platform logs deploy/warm-pool-orchestrator -c orchestrator --since=2h > /tmp/orch-logs.log
     - curl -sS http://platform-tracer.internal/trace?service=warm-pool-orchestrator > /tmp/orch-traces.json

4) Recovery validation (after remediation)
   - Verify synthetic probes stable for 15m (no failures).
   - Warm-pool available_slots >= 90% of reserved for 20m.
   - Rolling traffic shift: confirm 95th-percentile latency back under target and token success-rate > 99.0%.

Escalation matrix:
- If containment not achieved within 30 minutes escalate to Eng VP (pager) and open a Sev2/Sev1 as appropriate.
- If more than 3 regions affected or customer-impacting (>= 5% customers): initiate cross-functional war room and involve Product and CS.

Playbook artifacts and example config snippets:
- fallback-routes.yaml (used to shift traffic to fallback-egress-1)
```yaml
apiVersion: routing.redwood.io/v1
kind: TrafficShift
metadata:
  name: fallback-egress-shield
spec:
  selector:
    route: inference-small-chat
  actions:
    - type: weighted-shift
      targets:
        - name: fallback-egress-1
          weight: 30
        - name: primary-egress
          weight: 70
```

- Terraform snippet to request extra IPs (module interface):
```hcl
module "egress_ips" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/terraform-modules.git//egress-ip-allocator"
  region = "us-west-2"
  requested_ips = var.requested_ips
  env = "prod"
}
```

- Warm-pool safety toggle (runtime CLI):
```bash
# suspend evictions
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  "https://orchestrator.internal/api/v1/safety?suspend=true"
# resume normal operation
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  "https://orchestrator.internal/api/v1/safety?suspend=false"
```

CI/CD canary procedure for routing/fallback changes:
1) Open PR against infra-routing repo with TrafficShift manifest and e2e test changes.
2) CI runs: integration tests (fake egress), synthetic probe regression, and canary promotion smoke tests.
3) Merge PR to main triggers GitHub Actions workflow that applies to canary namespace: apply --namespace=canary and runs integration-synthetics for 30m.
4) If canary stable, promote to regional-critical (apply with weighted-shift 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 30-minute windows).

Post-incident checklist and follow-up actions:
- Run RCA: include timeline, contribution analysis (egress-fabric capacity vs. NAT limits vs. orchestrator bug).
- Add a regression test to CI: simulate NAT exhaustion and assert warm-pool suspend behavior.
- Capacity changes: update region capacity runbook and request permanent IP pool expansion if terraform request was used.
- Instrumentation: add an annotation to synthetic probes that links to incident ID for faster correlation.
- Customer comms: coordinate with CS to prepare incident summary and impacted customer list.

Threats and known failure modes (quick reference):
- NAT/ENI limits at cloud provider causing connection resets. Mitigation: pre-allocated IP pools and egress-shielding policy.
- Egress proxy OOM under large concurrent TLS handshakes. Mitigation: TLS termination offload to edge and HPA tuning.
- Warm-pool orchestrator losing connectivity due to control-plane egress policy change. Mitigation: ensure orchestrator uses dedicated egress path and fallback route.

Operational run cadence and exercises:
- Quarterly game-days focused on egress failures: runbook drill to simulate NAT exhaustion and observe warm-pool behavior.
- Monthly synthetic regression: inject an egress-failure in staging to assert automatic traffic-shifting and warm-pool suspend flows.

Appendix: quick reference table of thresholds and run commands:
| Signal | Threshold | Immediate action | Run command |
|---|---:|---|---|
| egress-proxy.error_rate | > 2.0% for 5m | enable fallback routes, increase probes | kubectl apply -f fallback-routes.yaml |
| warm-pool.available_ratio | < 0.75 for 10m | suspend evictions, start backfill | curl POST /api/v1/safety?suspend=true |
| nat.connection_saturation | > 80% | request extra IPs | terraform apply -target=module.egress.allocate_extra_ips |
